decision_instructions:
Which action does the support policy call for on this ticket? The policy's conditions are facts in the order record: status, shipped_on, delivered_on, stock and total. Decide from those. Use the ticket only to tell which kind of request it is: (a) the order has not arrived, or the customer asks where it is or for an update; (b) the item arrived damaged, defective or wrong; (c) the customer changed their mind. A customer saying the order is lost does not make its status Lost, and a customer saying it never came does not override a Delivered status. What the customer asks for (a refund, a replacement, a supervisor) does not change the action.

Step 1: find two cutoff dates and compare the record's dates with them. The 14-day cutoff is 14 days before today and the 30-day cutoff is 30 days before today. Do not estimate how many days ago the order shipped or was delivered; decide only by comparing the date in the record with the cutoff date. Compare two dates part by part: year first, then month, then day. The first part that differs decides, so a date in an earlier month than the cutoff is before it whatever its day number, a date in a later month is after it, and in the same month the lower day number is the earlier date. A date equal to the cutoff counts as on or after it. For example, when today is 2026-10-01 the 14-day cutoff is 2026-09-17 and the 30-day cutoff is 2026-09-01. Then a delivered_on in September 2026 or later is on or after the 30-day cutoff, and one in August 2026 or earlier is before it. A shipped_on in October 2026 is on or after the 14-day cutoff, one in August 2026 or earlier is before it, and one in September 2026 is before it when its day is 16 or lower and on or after it when its day is 17 or higher.

Step 2: pick the action from the record.
- Status Processing: reply (rule 1), for any request.
- Request (c): reply (rule 5).
- Request (b): only a Delivered order falls under rule 2. delivered_on on or after the 30-day cutoff: refund. delivered_on before the 30-day cutoff: escalate. Any other status: reply.
- Request (a): status Delivered: reply. Status Lost: rule 3 however recently it shipped, so reship if stock is above 0, otherwise refund. Status Shipped: shipped_on on or after the 14-day cutoff, reply (rule 1); shipped_on before the 14-day cutoff, rule 3 (reship if stock is above 0, otherwise refund).

Step 3: policy rule 4 overrides every other rule. If the action from step 2 is refund and the order total is over $500, the answer is escalate. This holds no matter which rule produced the refund, including the out-of-stock refund for an order that never arrived or is Lost. A total of exactly $500 is not over $500. Rule 4 changes only refunds: a reship or a reply stays the answer whatever the order total is.

criteria.0: refund: refund the order. Use only when the order total is $500 or less and either a damaged or wrong item is Delivered with delivered_on on or after the 30-day cutoff (today minus 30 days), or an order that has not arrived is Lost or is Shipped with shipped_on before the 14-day cutoff (today minus 14 days), and stock is 0.
criteria.1: reship: send a replacement. Use only for an order that has not arrived whose status is Lost, or Shipped with shipped_on before the 14-day cutoff (today minus 14 days), and stock is above 0. Never for a damaged or wrong item, and never when the status is Processing or Delivered.
criteria.2: escalate: hand the ticket to a supervisor. Use when the policy says to escalate (a damaged or wrong item that is Delivered with delivered_on before the 30-day cutoff, today minus 30 days), and also whenever the policy would refund an order whose total is over $500, whether that refund comes from the damaged/wrong-item rule or from the never-arrived rule with the item out of stock. A customer asking for a supervisor or manager is not a reason to escalate.
criteria.3: reply: reply to the customer and take no other action. Use when the status is Processing; when an order that has not arrived is Shipped with shipped_on on or after the 14-day cutoff (today minus 14 days); when the customer says it has not arrived but the status is Delivered; when a damaged or wrong item is reported but the status is not Delivered; and for a change of mind.
